draft.title: The circulatory system
card: The circulatory system moves blood around the body. The heart is a muscular pump that pushes blood through blood vessels.
carry blood away from the heart. Their walls are thick and strong, because blood leaves the heart under high pressure.
are the tiniest vessels, with walls only one cell thick. Oxygen and nutrients pass out of them into cells, and wastes such as carbon dioxide pass in.
carry blood back to the heart. Blood in veins is under lower pressure than in arteries.
draft.remember: The heart pumps blood out in arteries, through capillaries to the cells, and back in veins.

a.q: Which blood vessels have thin walls so materials can pass between the blood and the cells?
a.why: Capillaries have walls only one cell thick, so oxygen, nutrients and wastes can pass through them. Arteries have thick walls to cope with high pressure, so little passes through them.
a.clue: Think about which vessels are the tiniest.

b.q: Liam sprints and his leg muscle cells use up oxygen quickly. Where does oxygen leave his blood to enter these cells?
opts: In the capillaries in the muscle
In the arteries leaving the heart
In the veins returning to the heart
In the walls of the heart
b.why: Capillaries have walls one cell thick, so oxygen can pass out of them into the muscle cells. Arteries carry blood to the muscle, but their thick walls mean oxygen does not pass out of them.
b.clue: Which vessels sit right next to the cells?

b.best: In the capillaries in the muscle
